Hi Irene,

Thanks for the clear demo earlier — the team appreciated the walkthrough of streaming and the dedicated capacity options. A few follow-ups from our side so we can map to internal timelines: 

- Target latency SLO: 95th percentile tail <= 220ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) during peak (concurrency up to 230).
- Streaming behavior: need server-initiated chunking for partial responses (we stream long summaries). End-to-end token rate at peak estimated ~75k tokens/min.
- Failover: would like automatic fallback to a lower-cost model with slightly higher latency during rare capacity pressure events.

Can you confirm whether your reserved throughput planning should be expressed as tokens/sec per GPU, or as concurrent sessions per GPU for our workload shape? Also attach the matrix you mentioned for GPU choices and estimated reserved throughput — that will help procurement.

If possible, we’d like a short MMP (mutual action plan) that lists bench criteria, pilot acceptance tests, and expected timeline. Procurement will need an estimate of committed monthly capacity vs burstable.

Thanks — we’re aiming to decide by end of month.

Best,
Maria
Director of Product, BlueCrest Health

Thanks — writing up the short bench plan and a recommended reserved-slab mapping now. High-level engineering takeaways from our preliminary numbers: 

- For the 95p <=220ms target at <=128 tokens and concurrency ~230, an A40-class quantized instance (NVIDIA A40 / equivalent) averages ~180–210ms 95p at 1.2k tokens/sec sustained per GPU in our internal streaming microbench for the model family you saw. That gives ~15–20% headroom for burst.
- Hopper-architecture 80GB (H100-class) offers materially higher reserved throughput (~3.6k tokens/sec per GPU) and much lower 95p (~90–130ms), but incremental cost per committed slab is significant. H100 is a good fit if you want smaller slab counts and a simpler ops surface.
- If procurement wants lower dollar-commitment with predictable latency, we can propose a mixed-slate approach: a base reserved slab on A40-equivalent for steady load, plus a small H100 reserve to absorb tight tail pressure and reduce failover impact.

Validation approach (pilot bench steps):
1) Run streaming tail-latency sweep at target concurrency ranges (50 / 120 / 230) and measure 50/95/99p for short and long prompts (<=128, 256–512 tokens).
2) Token-rate soak at 75k tokens/min equivalent workload for 30m windows to validate thermal throttling and KV cache stability.
3) Failover simulation: induce a limited capacity pressure and validate automatic fallback quality + latency deltas and request routing.

I attached a compact CSV mapping tokens/sec to expected slabs and a short GPU tradeoff page (pdf already shared by Irene). I’ll be on the Tue 10am PT call and can walk through the bench plan.

-Karthik
Head of Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
